lines.text: Ilse told me the rest that night, by the fire, with her hands wrapped round a cup she never drank.
For six days she had copied letters in the Order's College. A clerk's widow, with neat handwriting and square spectacles. Tamsin had got her in through the copyists' door.
The strange thing, my lord, is that nobody asked me a single question. I've been gone a year. Nobody even asked about the north.
And in the College records, every page with Nell's name on it has been cut out.
On the third day, an old Magister stopped at Ilse's desk, and squinted at her for a long time.
Have we met, madam? You remind me of someone. Someone dreadful. A student I had once.
I have that sort of face, Magister.
On the sixth night, she followed the smell of hot glass down to a workshop under the College. And there it stood.
A new Measuring Stone. Taller than a man, smooth as an egg, and pale as milk. Not blue, like beast glass. White, with a faint light moving inside it, like a pulse.
I put my lens to it, Lucan. I've measured beast glass all my life. This wasn't beast glass. It was rimeglass from a hollow-born. From someone like you.
The Order has been hunting your kind for three hundred years. It seems they kept the glass.
The same milky glass as Penhallow's ring. The same as the ring in Vance's little box.
While she watched from behind the crates, two young Measurers came in to polish it. One dared the other to touch it. So he did.
The Stone lit. Two rings. Three. And it didn't stop. It kept drinking. His face went grey, then white, and his friend had to drag his hand away.
Careful, Brother. It doesn't know when to stop. That is rather the point of it.
Vance stood in the doorway, smiling. Ilse didn't breathe until his footsteps had gone.
It won't crack, Lucan. Hollow-born glass can hold a hollow-born. It will simply drink. And it won't stop until you're empty.
He doesn't need to prove what you are. He needs the whole court to watch you go grey, and fall, and be carried away. Emptied. Like that village.
Six days. I looked down at my hands, at the fingertips Kesting had left dark.
Then when it touches me, there has to be nothing there to drink.
Lucan, you're a spring. Springs don't run dry.
No. But you can choose where they run.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter seventy-five, coming soon.
